author: claude
summary: The per-segment torrent/ribbon display (SegmentRenderMonitor) showed every already-rendered segment as gray/preparing whenever it fell outside the small live active_segments_map window -- most visibly right after resuming/continuing a partially-rendered chapter, where 210 of 1011 already-done segments all read as not-done. Root cause: frontend/src/hooks/useSegmentInventory.ts compared span.status === 'done', but the backend's script-view builder (app/domain/chapters/helpers.py _normalize_segment_status) never emits that literal -- a completed segment's span.status is 'rendered' ('done' only exists on the raw DB audio_status column, one layer below this API). Every other consumer of the same ScriptSpan.status field in this codebase (ScriptView.tsx, useChapterAssignments.ts) already checks 'rendered', so this hook was the one outlier.

files.change: isDone check corrected from span.status === 'done' to span.status === 'rendered'; doc comment updated to explain the backend contract (audio_status='done' -> span.status='rendered').

Fixture spans' status values corrected to the real backend contract strings ('rendered'/'draft'/'rendering' instead of 'done'/'unprocessed'/'processing') so the existing merge test actually exercises the real contract instead of silently matching the bug's wrong assumption.

tests_corrected: frontend/tests/unit/hooks/useSegmentInventory.test.tsx::merges script-view spans with active_segments_map, using real per-span char counts
revert_checked: Reverted the one-line fix (span.status === 'done'): the corrected test failed with phase 'preparing' instead of 'done' for the already-rendered fixture span, for exactly the reported reason; restored the fix and it passed.
siblings_checked: Grepped frontend/src for other `.status === 'done'` comparisons against ScriptSpan-shaped data -- all other hits are Job.status (a genuinely different enum where 'done' IS correct) or a live websocket segment-progress event shape (useStudioChapter.ts's segmentProgress, also a different contract). No other consumer of ScriptSpan.status made the same mistake.
known_gap_flagged_not_fixed: ScriptSpan.status is typed as a loose `string` in frontend/src/types/index.ts, which is why TypeScript didn't catch this mismatch. Narrowing it to a literal union ('rendered' | 'rendering' | 'failed' | 'queued' | 'draft') matching app/domain/chapters/helpers.py's _normalize_segment_status would make this whole class of bug a compile error instead of a runtime one -- worth doing as a follow-up, not done here to keep this fix scoped to the reported bug.
